events.text:
I'll read the invoices.csv file and find which invoice id has the largest amount.
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="command">cd /tmp/tg-8vUnPF/work && cat invoices.csv</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="command">cd /tmp/tg-8vUnPF/work && head -20 invoices.csv && wc -l invoices.csv</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="command">cd /tmp/tg-8vUnPF/work && sort -t',' -k2 -nr invoices.csv | head -5</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>

Now let me analyze the data more carefully to find the maximum amount:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="command">cd /tmp/tg-8vUnPF/work && awk -F',' 'NR==1 {print; next} {print $1, $2}' invoices.csv | sort -k2 -nr | head -10</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>

Perfect! Let me verify this result:
<function_calls>
<invoke name="bash">
<parameter name="command">cd /tmp/tg-8vUnPF/work && awk -F',' 'NR>1 {if($2+0 > max) {max=$2; id=$1}} END {print "Invoice ID: " id ", Amount: " max}' invoices.csv</parameter>
</invoke>
</function_calls>

## Report

**Answer: Invoice ID `INV-0048` has the largest amount of `9999.99`**

**How I obtained it:**

1. Read the invoices.csv file in the working directory
2. Used `awk` to parse the CSV format and iterate through all rows
3. Compared the amount field (second column) for each row to find the maximum value
4. Tracked the corresponding invoice ID with that maximum amount
5. Verified the result by sorting the data by amount in descending order

The invoice with ID **INV-0048** contains the largest amount of **$9999.99**.
